about: Engine knobs, one row each, keyed by engine, and how `boltbeam tune MODEL --engine E` sets them on the machine it runs on (workflow/tune.py reads it; engines.<E>.adapter is the module that reads that engine's build, supplies its facts, runs its measured points and writes its command). kind: env (an environment variable), flag (a command-line flag), config (a key of a JSON config flag, a.b). requires: the build features the knob needs (the adapter's detect: llama.cpp the getenv names compiled into the build, vLLM the flags its installed arg parser adds and the Literal values of its config classes); a row whose feature is missing is not in that build. group: the engine's named extra the knob comes from (a local patch), for the words. applies: an expression over facts. derive: facts (a formula, instant), measured (a short real-text prefill sweep under --measure, over the row's axis knob; without it the facts value or the default stands, said so), default (left at the default, with the evidence why). bitwise false: the knob changes outputs (said beside it). Formulas use only the facts in workflow/tune.FACTS and the adapter's namespaced facts (ns.name), numbers, strings, + - * / //, comparisons, and/or/not, x if c else y, min, max, pow2_floor, gib_floor, gib_ceil, floor_to. Adding a knob is adding a row; adding an engine is a row under engines, its knobs and an adapter module.

llama-pinned-copy-stream.what: streams host-RAM experts to the GPU on a copy stream during prefill (v1: an L3-sized pinned ring; v2: a pinned copy made at load)

llama-moe-prefill.what: a parallel MoE routing sort, an MMQ tile-width knob and pinned staging for the server's state reads

llama-server-ckpt-min-head.what: no batch break and no checkpoint at a chat user-message start within the first N prompt tokens

knobs.name: --cache-ram
knobs.controls: llama-server's prompt cache in host RAM (MiB): it holds earlier requests' state in RAM
knobs.formula: 0 if (2 if llama_cpp.pin_in_build else 1) * host_expert_bytes + llama_cpp.host_tables_resident_bytes + llama_cpp.prompt_cache_default_bytes > usable_ram_bytes else None
knobs.reason: off when the host experts (counted twice when the build can pin them: the mmap pages the server still reads and a full pinned copy), the tables' resident rows and the default {llama_cpp.prompt_cache_default_gib:.0f} GiB prompt cache exceed the {usable_ram_gib:.0f} GiB usable RAM; the pin budget below gets that RAM
knobs.reason_default: kept: the host experts (and a full pinned copy, when the build can pin), the tables' resident rows and the {llama_cpp.prompt_cache_default_gib:.0f} GiB prompt cache fit the {usable_ram_gib:.0f} GiB usable RAM
knobs.not_applicable: no experts in host RAM, so the prompt cache competes with nothing this tool sets (boltbeam recommend says when to turn it off)
knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-expert-table-20261111.md Lever 4: the save costs ~80 ms per 10k prompt; the offload runs all used --cache-ram 0

knobs.name: -ub
knobs.controls: the chunk of prompt tokens one forward pass reads (llama-server --ubatch-size); -b is raised with it
knobs.reason: the chunk BoltBeam's prompt limit picks for this machine (the offload page's prompt setup): the smallest within the policy tie of the best; host experts are uploaded once per chunk, so bigger chunks upload less (with experts in RAM, 4096 measured 15% faster than 2048)
knobs.reason_default: llama-server's default: no prefill limit was computed here ({llama_cpp.plan_ubatch_why})

sweep.stop: two points in a row slower than the best by more than the tie

knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-expert-table-20261111.md Lever 3 (all-VRAM 10k: 2048 best, 2.7k: 4096), the offload match (-ub 4096) and the attribution audit (-ncmoe 12 pinned, 10k: -ub 4096 4,312 vs -ub 2048 3,745 tok/s wall)

knobs.name: -b
knobs.controls: the logical batch (llama-server --batch-size); a chunk (-ub) is never larger than it
knobs.reason: raised to -ub when -ub is larger (the command does it); larger than -ub measured no effect: -b 8192 at -ub 4096, 10k, 4,295 vs 4,312 tok/s (the server's head and near-end breaks still set the decode calls)
knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-expert-table-20261111.md attribution audit, arm GVf

knobs.name: LLAMA_WS
knobs.controls: the weight streamer on (1) or off (0)
knobs.reason: on: it only engages for prefill chunks of at least LLAMA_WS_MIN_TOKENS tokens with experts in host RAM; decode takes the stock path (measured unchanged, 24.6 vs 24.8 tok/s)
knobs.not_applicable: no experts in host RAM: the streamer has nothing to copy
knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-pinned-stream-20261111.md

knobs.name: LLAMA_WS_MIN_TOKENS
knobs.controls: the chunk size (tokens) from which a host expert tensor is uploaded whole on the copy stream instead of the stock routed-only, synchronous copy
knobs.reason: left at the patch's 1024: at -ub 4096 on a 10k prompt 256 and 1024 measured the same (4,329 vs 4,312 tok/s wall; the chat head batch is shorter than either). It decides only chunks smaller than it, so it matters only with small -ub (at -ub 256 and 512 the streamed path measured 1.8-1.9x the stock one)
knobs.not_applicable: no experts in host RAM: the streamer has nothing to copy
knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-expert-table-20261111.md attribution audit (GVa vs GV4: no change at -ub 4096; verdict: drop); llama-knob-derive-20261111.md (-ncmoe 12, all pinned: streamed 1.8-1.9x faster at -ub 256 and 512)

knobs.name: LLAMA_WS_PIN_GIB
knobs.controls: GiB of host experts copied once at load into pinned memory, which the GPU then reads at the full link rate
knobs.formula: gib_ceil(host_expert_bytes) if 2 * host_expert_bytes + llama_cpp.host_tables_resident_bytes + llama_cpp.prompt_cache_bytes <= usable_ram_bytes else max(0, gib_floor(usable_ram_bytes - host_expert_bytes - llama_cpp.host_tables_resident_bytes - llama_cpp.prompt_cache_bytes))
knobs.reason: a pinned copy is a second copy: the server's short chunks still read every host expert from the mmap, so all {host_expert_gib:.2f} GiB stay in the page cache. Pinned + host experts + tables' resident rows ({llama_cpp.host_tables_resident_gib:.2f} GiB) + prompt cache ({llama_cpp.prompt_cache_gib:.0f} GiB) must fit the {usable_ram_gib:.0f} GiB usable RAM ({ram_available_gib:.1f} GiB available when this ran, less the {ram_margin_gib:.0f} GiB margin). Conservative by the margin: on the 31 GB box the rule allows 1 GiB at -cmoe where 4 GiB measured best (+5% over none) and 8 GiB collapsed. Run it with no other model server holding RAM. What it pins is whole expert tensors in load order, not experts by use: a measured routing profile (boltbeam routing MODEL --engine E{llama_cpp.routing_note}) says which experts a pin should hold first, which this patch cannot do yet, so that is advice only, not a setting
knobs.not_applicable: no experts in host RAM: nothing to pin
knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-pinned-stream-20261111.md v2: -ncmoe 12/18/24 all pinned best (1.58-1.91x stock); -cmoe 4 GiB best, 8/12 GiB collapsed (18-42k major faults per request) on 31 GB; kept by the attribution audit's verdict

knobs.name: GGML_CUDA_WS_RING_MIB
knobs.controls: the pinned staging ring the unpinned host experts are memcpy'd through (MiB)
knobs.reason: a quarter of the {l3_mib:.0f} MiB L3 the copying core shares ({l3_source}), a power of two: the memcpy's writes stay in cache and the DMA reads them from there, so staging is not DRAM-bound twice. The quarter is the measured best on one L3 size (32 MiB); other sizes are extrapolated by it
knobs.reason_default: the patch's 8 MiB: the L3 size could not be read ({l3_source})
knobs.not_applicable: no experts in host RAM: nothing is staged
knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-pinned-stream-20261111.md tuning on a 32 MiB L3: 8 MiB (1 x 8) 1,661 tok/s; 2 MiB 1,563; 16 MiB 1,463-1,485; 512 MiB 612

knobs.name: GGML_CUDA_WS_CHUNK_KIB
knobs.controls: one staging copy's size (KiB): the ring holds ring / chunk copies in flight
knobs.reason: the ring in eight chunks, so the CPU fills one while the DMA drains the others (measured: 8 chunks beat 4 at the same ring)
knobs.reason_default: the patch's 1024 KiB: the L3 size could not be read ({l3_source})
knobs.not_applicable: no experts in host RAM: nothing is staged
knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-pinned-stream-20261111.md tuning: 1 MiB x 8 1,661 vs 4 MiB x 4 1,463, 512 KiB x 4 1,563

knobs.name: GGML_CUDA_WS_SLOTS
knobs.controls: device slots the streamer uploads ahead into (prefetch depth)
knobs.reason: 4 slots run ~1.3 layers ahead, enough to overlap; 8 measured slower (1,444 vs 1,485 tok/s) and cost VRAM. Streaming further ahead is not a lever: Strata's own stream-ahead off measured the same (6,039 vs 6,045 tok/s)
knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-pinned-stream-20261111.md T2 tuning; llama-expert-table-20261111.md attribution audit (d2): stream-ahead 0, verdict: drop

knobs.name: GGML_CUDA_WS_THREADS
knobs.controls: CPU threads per staging memcpy
knobs.reason: the staging copy is bound by RAM, not by one core: 2 and 4 threads measured slower (880 and 305 vs 1,661 tok/s)
knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-pinned-stream-20261111.md T2 tuning

knobs.name: GGML_CUDA_WS_PAGEABLE
knobs.controls: 1: no pinned ring, the copy stream reads the pageable mmap directly
knobs.reason: a debugging switch: pageable copies measured 751 vs 1,661 tok/s with the ring
knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-pinned-stream-20261111.md

knobs.name: GGML_CUDA_MMID_PAR_MIN
knobs.controls: the chunk size (tokens) from which the parallel MoE routing sort replaces the serial one
knobs.reason_default: the patch's crossover (outputs are bit-identical either way; at 10k it cut mm_ids 82 -> 26 ms); confirmed by --measure
knobs.not_applicable: the model has no experts: there is no routing sort

sweep.stop: the parallel arm faster by more than the tie at two points in a row

knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-expert-table-20261111.md (first section)

knobs.name: GGML_CUDA_MMQ_ID_J
knobs.controls: forces the MMQ column-tile width for MoE products (unset: llama.cpp's own rule)
knobs.reason: a sweep knob, left unset: wider tiles were measured slower (J=128 at -ub 2048: expert MMQ 354 -> 395 ms); llama.cpp's mean-columns rule was already the best of the sweep
knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-expert-table-20261111.md Lever 2

knobs.name: GGML_CUDA_BATCH_GET_STAGING
knobs.controls: a reused pinned staging buffer for the server's state reads (checkpoints, prompt-cache saves) instead of pinning each destination
knobs.reason: on: each fresh 112 MiB pin cost ~40 ms per checkpoint; staging measured +4.5% at 10k, results bit-identical
knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-expert-table-20261111.md Lever 3

knobs.name: GGML_CUDA_BATCH_GET_STAGING_MAX_MIB
knobs.controls: the largest state read (MiB) that goes through the staging buffer; larger ones take the old path
knobs.reason: a cap on pinned memory: the largest staged span measured 448 MiB with the prompt cache on (128 MiB with --cache-ram 0), under the cap
knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-expert-table-20261111.md Lever 4

knobs.name: LLAMA_SERVER_CKPT_MIN_HEAD
knobs.controls: no batch break and no context checkpoint at a chat user-message start within the first N prompt tokens (0: stock, a break at every user start)
knobs.reason: 256 with experts in host RAM: the chat template's short head (42 tokens here) otherwise runs as its own batch, which uploads every host layer's experts per expert from pageable memory (2.6 GB, ~250 ms) and then takes a checkpoint sync; measured +16% at 10k (4,551 -> 5,278 tok/s wall) and +53% at 2.7k (3,089 -> 4,731). Outputs are not bitwise identical (the batch boundaries move): the first argmax divergences are near-ties (top-2 probabilities within 0.01-0.09), the same envelope as stock -ub 2048 vs 4096; checkpoint restore still works
knobs.reason_default: stock (0): every expert is on the GPU, where the head batch costs no expert upload; not measured there
knobs.evidence: ~/storage/boltbeam-runs/llama-expert-table-20261111.md 'Fix found during the audit' (combined3 vs combined2, chat text, n=6) and the verdict's cause #1; tools/patches/llama-server-ckpt-min-head.patch

knobs.name: --max-model-len
knobs.controls: the longest context vLLM serves; it must find KV cache room for one sequence this long at start
knobs.reason: the {context_tokens}-token context this setup is sized for (--context): the rows below fit the KV cache for it, and unset vLLM takes the model's whole context and must fit that
knobs.evidence: vllm/config/model.py:217 (default None: the model's own length); vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:999 (check_enough_kv_cache_memory); vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:951

knobs.name: --gpu-memory-utilization
knobs.controls: the share of the GPU's total memory vLLM takes for weights, activations and the KV cache
knobs.formula: max(0.01, floor_to((gpu_free_bytes - GiB) / gpu_total_bytes, 0.01)) if (gpu_free_bytes - GiB) / gpu_total_bytes >= vllm.min_share and gpu_free_bytes - GiB < 0.92 * gpu_total_bytes else None
knobs.reason: the free share of the GPU now ({gpu_free_gib:.1f} of {gpu_total_gib:.1f} GiB) less 1 GiB for vLLM's own CUDA context, which exists before vLLM reads free memory: vLLM refuses to start when free memory is under utilization x total, and another program holds the rest. It reads the GPU now: run it with nothing else on the GPU for the share the model will have. A share below what the weights need (plus 2 GiB for activations) is never set: vLLM's default stands, and it names the shortfall itself at start.{vllm.gpu_warning}
knobs.reason_default: vLLM's default: {gpu_free_gib:.1f} of {gpu_total_gib:.1f} GiB is free; a lower share is derived only when the free memory is under 0.92 of the total and still holds the weights plus 2 GiB for activations.{vllm.gpu_warning}
knobs.reason_missing: vLLM's default: the GPU's memory could not be read here, so the share is not checked against what is free
knobs.evidence: vllm/config/cache.py:103 (default 0.92); vllm/v1/worker/utils.py:543-555 (free < utilization x total refuses to start); vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:1326

knobs.name: --kv-cache-dtype
knobs.controls: the KV cache's element type (auto: the model's, bf16 here)
knobs.formula: 'fp8' if model_weight_bytes + kv_bytes_per_token * context_tokens > vllm.gpu_share * gpu_total_bytes else None
knobs.reason: fp8: the weights ({model_weight_gib:.2f} GiB) and a {context_tokens}-token bf16 KV cache ({kv_bytes_per_token:,.0f} bytes per token) do not fit vLLM's {vllm.gpu_share} share of {gpu_total_gib:.1f} GiB; fp8 halves the cache. Quality is not measured here
knobs.reason_missing: auto (vLLM's): the GPU's memory could not be read here, so the fit of a {context_tokens}-token cache is not checked
knobs.reason_default: auto: the weights ({model_weight_gib:.2f} GiB) and a {context_tokens}-token cache at the model's type fit vLLM's {vllm.gpu_share} share of {gpu_total_gib:.1f} GiB (activations and graphs not counted)
knobs.not_applicable: the model has no per-token KV cache
knobs.evidence: vllm/config/cache.py:39-58 (CacheDType), :123 (default auto); vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:1334; the same fit as workflow/recommend.context_figures

knobs.name: --cpu-offload-gb
knobs.controls: GiB of weights per GPU kept in pinned host memory and read by the GPU over the link (UVA zero-copy) in each forward
knobs.formula: min(gib_ceil(model_weight_bytes + vllm.kv_bytes_per_token * context_tokens - vllm.gpu_share * gpu_total_bytes), gib_floor(usable_ram_bytes) - vllm.process_headroom_gib)
knobs.reason: what the weights ({model_weight_gib:.2f} GiB) and the {context_tokens}-token KV cache need beyond vLLM's {vllm.gpu_share} share of {gpu_total_gib:.1f} GiB: a lower bound (activations and graphs not counted). The offloaded weights live in pinned host RAM, so it is capped at the {usable_ram_gib:.0f} GiB usable less {vllm.process_headroom_gib} GiB kept free for the vLLM process itself (a margin, not a measurement). A model that does not fit the GPU share plus that RAM is refused before this row
knobs.not_applicable: the weights and the {context_tokens}-token KV cache fit the GPU: nothing to offload
knobs.evidence: vllm/config/offload.py:23-32 (cpu_offload_gb, UVA); vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:1402

knobs.name: --cpu-offload-params
knobs.controls: which parameters (name segments) the offload takes first; unset: any, in load order, up to --cpu-offload-gb
knobs.reason: experts: a decode step reads only the routed experts of each layer, while it reads every dense weight, so offloading experts moves the least-read bytes over the link when writing replies. A long prompt touches nearly every expert, so prompts read the offloaded bytes in full either way
knobs.reason_default: unset: a dense model reads every weight each forward, so no subset is cheaper to keep in host memory
knobs.evidence: vllm/config/offload.py:34-44 (segment match, 'mlp.experts.w2_weight' matches 'experts'); vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:1404

knobs.name: --offload-backend
knobs.controls: how offloaded weights reach the GPU: uva (zero-copy reads of pinned host memory) or prefetch (whole layers in groups, copied ahead asynchronously, --offload-group-size)
knobs.reason: auto selects uva when only --cpu-offload-gb is set; prefetch is the other backend, set by layer groups instead of GiB. The two are not measured against each other here, so vLLM's pick stands
knobs.evidence: vllm/model_executor/offloader/base.py:156-162 (auto: prefetch if offload_group_size > 0, uva if cpu_offload_gb > 0); vllm/config/offload.py:47-75 (prefetch), :83; vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:1400

knobs.name: --max-num-batched-tokens
knobs.controls: the most tokens one engine step schedules: the chunk a long prompt is prefilled in (chunked prefill)
knobs.formula: 16384 if gpu_total_bytes >= 160 * GiB else 8192 if gpu_total_bytes >= 70 * GiB else 2048
knobs.reason: vLLM's own server default for a {gpu_total_gib:.0f} GiB GPU (2048 under 70 GiB, 8192 from 70, 16384 from 160; not 8192 on an A100; its offline LLM class uses larger ones), written out so the command keeps it; a bigger chunk takes fewer steps and more activation memory: --measure sweeps it on real text
knobs.reason_default: unset: vLLM picks by the GPU's size, which could not be read here; --measure sweeps it on real text

sweep.stop: two points in a row slower than the best by more than the tie

knobs.evidence: vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:2858-2885 (by GPU memory and usage context), :1668 (the flag)

knobs.name: speculative_config.num_speculative_tokens
knobs.controls: MTP: draft tokens per step from the checkpoint's own multi-token-prediction head (unset: no speculation)
knobs.reason: the draft count measured on this chip (workflow/recommend: the largest k that beats the next smaller one by more than the tie and loses at no measured depth)
knobs.reason_default: unset: not measured for this model on this chip ({vllm.mtp_why}). Measured elsewhere: 1.6x at k=3 on the 27B on the 5090
knobs.not_applicable: the checkpoint has no MTP head
knobs.evidence: vllm/config/speculative.py:39-66 (MTP model types), :394 (num_speculative_tokens); vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:1793; workflow/recommend.MTP_NOTE
